question: Fill in the blank:Ghoomar was recognized among the world’s leading local dances in the year _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghoomar** is a traditional folk dance of **Rajasthan** that is deeply rooted in the state’s culture and heritage.
 
• In the year **2013**, Ghoomar gained international recognition and was listed among the **world’s leading local dances**, showcasing its cultural significance on a global platform.
 
• This dance form is primarily performed by women who wear traditional **ghagra (long skirts)** and adorn themselves with intricate jewelry, representing the colorful and vibrant essence of Rajasthan.
 
• Ghoomar is performed on special occasions like **weddings, festivals, and religious ceremonies**, and is considered a symbol of joy and celebration.
 
• Its inclusion in the list of leading dances in **2013** highlighted the importance of preserving and promoting regional art forms globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Ghoomar:**

 
 
• The dance originated in **Marwar**, Rajasthan, and was traditionally performed by the **Bhil tribe** to worship Goddess Saraswati.
 
• Over time, it became popular among the **Rajput community** and was integrated into royal festivities.
 
 
 
• **Features of Ghoomar Dance:**
 
 
• The dance involves **graceful twirling movements** that showcase the flowing ghagras worn by the performers.
 
• It is accompanied by traditional **folk music**, including songs that narrate tales of Rajasthan’s culture and history.
 
• The performers maintain **rhythmic hand and foot movements**, symbolizing elegance and tradition.
 
 
 
• **Global Significance:**
 
 
• Ghoomar has been performed at various **international cultural events**, enhancing its global appeal and recognition.
 
• Its inclusion in the list of leading local dances in **2015** brought attention to the importance of preserving such traditional art forms.
 
 
 
• **Other Famous Folk Dances of India:**
 
 
• **Bihu:** A folk dance from Assam, performed during the Bihu festival.
 
• **Garba:** A traditional dance from Gujarat, performed during Navratri celebrations.
 
• **Lavani:** A vibrant dance form from Maharashtra, known for its energetic performances.
 
• **Bhangra:** A lively folk dance from Punjab, performed during harvest festivals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**

 
 
• Several traditional dances, including some from India, have been recognized as part of UNESCO’s **Intangible Cultural Heritage**, emphasizing the need to preserve them.
 
• While Ghoomar is not yet on the UNESCO list, its global recognition in **2015** has paved the way for similar efforts.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Folk Art:**
 
 
• The Indian government and cultural organizations have been actively working to **promote traditional art forms** through events, festivals, and media.
 
• Such initiatives ensure that folk dances like Ghoomar remain an integral part of India’s **cultural identity**.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Tourism:**
 
 
• Folk dances like Ghoomar attract **tourists** from around the world, contributing to India’s cultural tourism industry.
 
• Rajasthan, in particular, is known for its vibrant culture, with Ghoomar performances being a major highlight for visitors.
